evidence: Cic. Off. 2.83: habitent grātīs in aliēnō
Mart. 5.16.10: tantum grātīs pāgina nostra placet
terms.comment: Contracted from grātiīs, the form of Plautus and Terence (Lewis & Short). “It costs nothing” is grātīs cōnstat (Sen. Ep. 104.34; Cic. Verr. 2.5.48, Lewis & Short); to give away free, grātīs dare (Mart. 14.175.2, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Suet. Cal. 26: grātuīta in Circō loca, free seats (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Free as against paid for: free seats, an interest-free loan (pecūnia grātuīta, Plin. Ep. 3.11.2, Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: freedom cannot be had for nothing

phrases.latin: et tantum grātīs pāgina nostra placet
phrases.english: and my pages only please when they are free
